Family Card | Social Security Policy Support (SSPS) Programme

# Family Card

March 11, 2026

The Family Card is a database-driven digital identification and social protection instrument designed to deliver regular financial assistance directly to vulnerable households. More than just a cash transfer mechanism, it is envisioned as a universal social safety platform that integrates multiple welfare services under a single identity instrument.

```
Core Philosophy"Family is the core unit of development, not the individual." The programme shifts the design logic of social protection from targeting individuals to supporting the household as a whole; recognizing that poverty, food insecurity, health shocks, and economic vulnerability are experienced collectively.
```

Programme at a Glance

| Implementing Ministry | Ministry of Social Welfare, Government of Bangladesh |
| --- | --- |
| Programme Type | Digital cash transfer + subsidised commodities access |
| Cash Benefit | BDT 2,000 â 2,500 per family per month |
| Target Coverage | Up to 2 crore (20 million) families nationally |
| Pilot Launch | March 10; covering 6,500 families in 14 upazilas |
| Transfer Mechanism | Mobile Financial Services (bKash, Nagad, Rocket) or bank account |
| Card Issuance | One card per household; issued in the female headâs name |
| Selection Method | Proxy Means Test (PMT) scoring + door-to-door data collection |
| Long-Term Vision | Universal Social ID Card for every citizen by 2030 |
| Fiscal Target | Social protection budget raised to 3% of GDP by 2028 |

## ðµ Direct Cash Transfer

- Monthly BDT 2,000-2,500 deposited digitally
- No intermediaries
- Reduced corruption risk.

## ð Universal Social ID

A single smart card enabling access to

- Subsidized food
- Education stipends
- Agri-support by 2030.

## ð Dynamic Social Registry

- A unified database replacing fragmented records
- Integrating 99 existing programmes across the ministries/divisions

Inclusion Criteria

- Rural families owning 0.50 acres or less of homestead and cultivable land
- Households assessed as poor or ultra-poor based on income and asset evaluation
- Landless, homeless, persons with disabilities, and marginalized communities (including Hijra, Bede, and small ethnic groups)

Exclusion Criteria

- Any family member who is a regular government employee or pensioner
- Households with a commercial license or large business operations
- Families possessing a car or air conditioner

```
Priority GroupsImplementation begins with the most vulnerable segments; the ultra-poor, homeless, persons with disabilities, and socially marginalized communities. Despite the programme's universal ambition, targeting starts at the bottom of the economic ladder.
```

# Govt targets database of 4.45cr families under family card programme

 Nationwide data collection begins with over 66,000 enumerators; completion target set for December 

 Published : 12 October 2026 

 Updated : 12 October 2026, 22:15 

Photo: PID

The government has set a target to collect data from an estimated 4.45 crore families and add them to a database by December, as nationwide data collection under the Family Card programme began today.

A total of 66,815 data collectors and 6,681 supervisors have been deployed for the exercise, Social Welfare Minister Prof Dr AZM Zahid Hossain said at a press conference at the Information Secretariat on Monday.

State Minister for Social Welfare Farjana Sharmin was also present.

Dr Zahid noted that the prime minister inaugurated the pilot phase of the Family Card programme on March 10.

During the pilot phase, which ran through June 2026, data was collected from 112,094 families in 57 units across 55 upazilas and city corporation areas in 44 districts under all eight divisions, he said.

Based on Proxy Means Test scores, 71,831 eligible beneficiaries were selected and provided with family cards and allowances.

The minister said full-scale implementation of the programme began in July, with Tk 14,500 crore allocated for its execution in the 2026-27 fiscal year.

Dr Zahid said ensuring women's economic independence and advancing national development and social justice were among the government's key commitments.

# 1.61Cr families to be covered under Family Card scheme by 2030: State minister | The Business Standard
URL: https://www.tbsnews.net/bangladesh/161cr-families-be-covered-under-family-card-scheme-2030-state-minister-1488176
Published: 2026-07-14
Author: TBS Report

TBS Report 14 July, 2026, 05:15 pm Last modified: 14 July, 2026, 05:16 pm 

## Around 4.10 crore families will be counted to build a modern database under the DSR system, with the aim of bringing 1.61 crore families under its coverage by the 2029-30 fiscal year 

 TBS Report 14 July, 2026, 05:15 pm Last modified: 14 July, 2026, 05:16 pm 

 File Photo of family card. Photo: BSS 

The government aims to bring 1.61 crore families under the Family Card scheme by 2030 and will distribute 41 lakh new cards nationwide in the current 2026-27 fiscal year, said State Minister for Social Welfare Farzana Sharmin Putul today (14 July).

She made the remarks in parliament on behalf of Social Welfare Minister Abu Zafar Md Zahid Hossain while responding to a question from Dhaka-18 lawmaker SM Jahangir Hossain during the question and answer session.

The state minister said a nationwide integrated family census will begin at the start of the current fiscal year. Around 4.10 crore families will be counted to build a modern database under the DSR system, with the aim of bringing 1.61 crore families under its coverage by the 2029-30 fiscal year.

Beneficiaries will be selected through field-level surveys and Proxy Means Test (PMT) scores.

She said allowances have so far been distributed through Family Cards to 69,387 women-headed families under a pilot project implemented in three phases across 56 units in 55 upazilas of 44 districts. Field-level information is also being updated regularly.

According to the government's initial plan, 41 lakh new Family Cards will be issued during the current fiscal year. Upazila Nirbahi Officers have been instructed to recruit data collectors, and the Family Card Census Guidelines, 2026 have already been issued.

The draft Family Card Implementation Policy, 2026 has also been approved by the cabinet committee and sent to the Department of Printing and Publications for gazette notification.

Regarding Dhaka-18, the state minister said the pilot programme has started in parts of the Karail, Sattala, Bhashantek, Olimiar Tek and Baganbari slums under Dhaka North City Corporation.

She said Family Cards will be distributed more widely in Uttara and surrounding areas during the current fiscal year after the family census is completed. Ward-wise beneficiary lists will also be provided to the local lawmaker's office after the census.

# 45m families to be included in Family Card database: Dr Zahid | News Flash
URL: https://www.bssnews.net/news-flash/434048
Published: 2026-10-12

45m families to be included in Family Card database: Dr Zahid | News Flash

BSS 12 Oct 2026, 17:40 Update : 12 Oct 2026, 17:45

#### 45m families to be included in Family Card database: Dr Zahid

Social Welfare and Women and Children Affairs Minister Professor Dr. AZM Zahid Hossain spoke at PID at the Bangladesh Secretariat in Dhaka. Photo: BSS

DHAKA, Oct 12, 2026 (BSS) - Data collection at the household level has begun today across the country under the government's priority 'Family Card' program, aimed at ensuring women's empowerment, their economic emancipation and self-reliance.

Through this initiative, data on approximately 45 million families across the country will be integrated into a single digital database.

Professor Dr. AZM Zahid Hossain, Minister for Social Welfare and Women and Children Affairs, disclosed this information today at a press conference at the Press Information Department (PID) at Bangladesh Secretariat here.

State Minister for Social Welfare Farzana Sharmin Putul, Ministryâs Secretary Dr. Mohammad Abu Yousuf and Principal Information Officer (PIO) Syed Abdal Ahmad, along with officials concerned from the ministry and the Department of Social Services, were present at the conference.

During the briefing, the Social Welfare Minister stated that as part of the Family Card initiative, the process of collecting data through direct door-to-door visits began nationwide today.

A total of 66,815 trained data collectors and 6,681 supervisors have been deployed for this task. The data collection process is scheduled to conclude by November 30 and it will be ready by December.

Dr. Zahid Hossain said, "Ordinary citizens need not to run after government offices or individuals to obtain a Family Card, government data collectors will visit the doorstep of every family directly. Eligible families will automatically be identified from the database using a fully scientific Proxy Means Test (PMT) method."

In this context, he said, "There is no scope for political influence, nepotism or the use of unfair means to get a family card."

He said, initially out of 45 million households between 16 million and 21 million families categorized as ultra-poor, poor or low-income will be identified as eligible for the allowance based on their PMT scores.

Dr. Zahid Hossain announced that 4.1 million women, who are heads of households, are being brought under this allowance scheme in the current 2026-27 fiscal year.

All eligible families will receive this benefit in phases over the next four years. A total of Taka 14,500 crore has been allocated for the program's being implemented this fiscal year.

The minister noted that the 'Family Card' issued to the women would be highly secure. Equipped with dual-chip, QR code and Near Field Communication (NFC) technologies, the card will be linked to the government's 'Taka Pay' payment scheme.
